newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Ciller rebuffs Gaddafi criticism.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Ciller rebuffs Gaddafi criticism.

text.p: Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller rebuffed sharp criticism by Libyan leader Muammer Gaddafi over Turkey's month-long incursion into northern Iraq and military cooperation with Israel, the foreign ministry said on Friday.

"Gaddafi's...inappropriate expressions are not in harmony with the rules of respect and politeness of international relations. We strongly reject Gaddafi's expressions," she said in a statement faxed to Reuters on Friday.

Gaddafi attacked the Turkish army on Wednesday, saying it was ruled by Jews. "The Jews who rule the Turkish army made it (take a stand) against the Arabs," he said in a speech in the Libyan city of Derna.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas fighting for self-rule in southeastern Turkey.
Most Arab states protested against the Turkish incursion, calling for the respect of integrity and unity of Iraqi soil.
Arab countries were also worried about Turkish-Israeli defence deals signed by the two states in the last 18 months.
